reading.body:
Montana's data center footprint consists of two known facilities, neither of which reports measurable power draw, leaving the state effectively absent from AI infrastructure at this time.

Both facilities serve administrative or general IT purposes rather than compute-intensive workloads. One is operated by the State of Montana government, and one is a private data management provider. Neither name suggests the high-density power infrastructure, redundant cooling, or large-scale fiber interconnects that AI training or inference at scale requires.

The total reported capacity is zero megawatts, which likely reflects absent reporting rather than genuinely zero power consumption. The data does not cover colocation capacity, planned construction, utility interconnection requests, or land permits, so it cannot say whether Montana is being considered for future build-out. What it does confirm is that as of the generation date, Montana contributes nothing measurable to the compute layer that AI scaling depends on.
